hints.title: Median Partition Alternation Obstacle
hints.text: Reorder an array so elements alternate strictly smaller and larger than their neighbors. How can separating elements above and below the median avoid adjacent duplicate collisions?

hints.title: Reverse Split Placement Invariant
hints.text: Placing the smaller half into even slots and larger half into odd slots from right to left keeps any duplicate median values far apart.

hints.title: Sorted Reverse Interleaving Procedure
hints.text: Sort a copy of the numbers. Distribute the smaller half into even positions from end to start, and the larger half into odd positions from end to start. This prevents equal median elements from being placed in consecutive indices.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def wiggleSort(self, nums: List[int]) -> None:
        arr = sorted(nums)
        n = len(nums)
        mid = (n - 1) // 2
        nums[::2] = arr[mid::-1]
        nums[1::2] = arr[:mid:-1]
```

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy swapping often causes identical adjacent elements when duplicates equal to the median exist.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting a copy requires O(N log N) time and O(N) extra space while guaranteeing correct alternate interleaving.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand why placing sorted halves from high to low indices prevents median collisions.
